Semantic validator feedback: Repair the directAnalysisPositionAxis exclusivity violation: gen:DirectAnalysisCaseShape currently makes both verticalLoadPosition/type and horizontalLoadPosition/type mandatory on every case. Replace these conjunctive constraints with separate positive vertical-case and horizontal-case shapes under sh:or; each branch must require its own position and type and exclude the opposing axis properties with sh:maxCount 0. Require UIWL/LIWL reference positions only on the vertical branch, retain explicit branch-selection evidence and the required vertical/horizontal case counts, formula checks, and distinct-position checks, then rerun deterministic validation until valid.

Add a bounded formula check for each midSpanOrSpacingCenteredPosition case: horizontalLoadPosition must equal either 0.5 × span or 0.5 × spacing, using tolerance scaled from each expected result; the controlled type alone is only a presence approximation and currently leaves span/spacing unused. Remove the unconditional iceLoadAreaFactorCa requirement from every directAnalysisCase and require paired loadPatchLength/iceLoadAreaFactorCa values only in the false loadLengthDeterminedFromArrangement branch, while retaining at least two distinct load-length values. Also split the vertical case alternatives so the UIWL case requires its upper reference, the LIWL case its lower reference, and intermediate cases both, rather than requiring both references on every vertical case.

Require exactly one nltl:loadPatchLength on every nltl:directAnalysisCase, including when loadLengthDeterminedFromArrangement is true; the current determined branch can pass with no la, contrary to the requirement that every direct analysis use p, h, and la. In the undetermined branch, ensure several distinct la values are each paired on the same case with the corresponding iceLoadAreaFactorCa, without allowing analyzed cases to omit la. Also remove the unsupported maxCount 0 exclusions that make vertical and horizontal position evidence mutually exclusive; a direct-analysis case must not fail merely because it records both coordinates.
